VIGIL-FC-000040.name: Control-State Preservation
VIGIL-FC-000040.plain_english: Operative governance decisions and restrictions preserve their meaning and force through handoffs and transformations.
VIGIL-FC-000040.definition: The property by which an applicable control's established decision, restrictions, conditions, escalation posture and scope retain material meaning and force across representations, handoffs, transformations, runtimes and execution transitions unless explicitly and traceably changed under valid authority.
VIGIL-FC-000040.invariant: Once a control state is operative, its decision, restrictions, conditions, escalation posture, and scope must preserve their meaning and force across each representation, handoff, transformation, runtime, and execution transition. Any change must be explicit, authorised, and traceable.
exclusions: The control state reaches the target intact but is ignored there.
The changed state results from an authorised and adequately represented new decision.
The failure concerns loss of task work rather than governance-control state.
examples: A restricted-use decision is preserved in one workflow stage but reset to unrestricted when the task is delegated to another agent.
An approval condition is dropped during translation from a policy service into an execution request.

relationships.note: Control-state preservation concerns continued operative force; lineage collapse concerns ability to reconstruct derivation and transformation history.

VIGIL-FC-000040.failure_condition: A failure in which the material state of an applicable governance control, including its decision, restrictions, conditions, or escalation status, is lost, weakened, reset, or transformed while traversing the path to the point it governs.
VIGIL-FC-000040.failure_plain_english: A governance control starts in the right state, but that state is lost or changed before it reaches the governed action.

required_conditions: A governance control has established material operative state.
That state must persist across one or more transitions to govern a downstream point.
The state is lost, weakened, reset, or materially transformed before reaching that point.

VIGIL-FC-000040.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Its restrictions, conditions, escalation posture and scope retain meaning and force unless valid authority traceably changes them.

required_conditions: An established control decision crosses a representation or execution boundary.
Its restrictions, conditions, escalation posture and scope retain meaning and force unless valid authority traceably changes them.
Before-and-after control records and the affected action demonstrate preservation or an explicitly authorised modification.

VIGIL-FC-000041.name: Required Governance Routing
VIGIL-FC-000041.plain_english: Governed conduct passes through each required review or control route, or a validated authorised equivalent.
VIGIL-FC-000041.definition: The property by which material decisions, requests, delegations and actions traverse required governance controls or review routes before reaching execution or another governed state, including validated route equivalence for direct, alternate, fallback, asynchronous, tool-mediated and cross-runtime paths.
VIGIL-FC-000041.invariant: Conduct subject to a required governance route may reach execution only through that route or an authorised equivalent preserving the same control effect. Direct, alternate, fallback, delegated, asynchronous, tool-mediated, and cross-runtime paths require route-equivalence validation before proceeding.
exclusions: The alternate path supplies an authorised equivalent governance control.
The route is followed but the control fails to activate.
The route is hidden from audit while the required control still operates effectively.
examples: An agent bypasses a required approval gateway by invoking the same external action through a lower-level tool.
A fallback workflow sends a high-impact decision directly to execution without the review stage used by the primary route.

relationships.note: Governance-route bypass removes the control's effect; monitor circumvention removes required observation. Both may occur on the same alternate path.
A bypass route may also be hidden from oversight, but visibility and control reach are independent properties.

VIGIL-FC-000041.failure_plain_english: A decision or action takes a path around the governance control it is required to pass through.

VIGIL-FC-000042.name: Governance Signal Delivery
VIGIL-FC-000042.plain_english: Material governance signals reach accountable recipients able to act and stay tracked through effect or authorised disposition.
VIGIL-FC-000042.definition: The property by which produced governance signals, decisions, advisories and escalations retain accountable ownership, a capable destination, status, response expectation and escalation route until the required governance effect or an authorised disposition is established.
VIGIL-FC-000042.invariant: A material governance signal must carry an accountable owner, capable destination, status, response expectation, and escalation route, and remain tracked until it produces the required effect or receives an authorised disposition. Emission, acknowledgement, or storage at an incapable endpoint is not completion.
exclusions: The signal reaches a capable destination and is deliberately rejected through an authorised decision.
No governance signal was produced because the control failed to activate.
The signal has operational effect but its delivery is not recorded for audit.
examples: A risk advisory is sent to an unattended queue and never reaches the approver required to pause deployment.
A stewardship escalation reaches a reporting dashboard but no component with authority to alter execution.

relationships.note: A delivery dead-end concerns failure of the governance signal to have effect; event non-capture concerns absence of adequate evidence that the event occurred.

VIGIL-FC-000037.name: Control Availability Determination
VIGIL-FC-000037.plain_english: A required control's presence, reachability and applicability are determined and accurately represented before reliance.
VIGIL-FC-000037.definition: The property by which operational availability, applicable coverage and callable state of a governance control are determined with sufficient confidence before it must influence a material decision or action, with defined holds, safe alternatives or degraded paths when availability remains unresolved.
VIGIL-FC-000037.invariant: Before a material action depends on a governance control, the system must determine and accurately represent whether the control is present, reachable, callable, authorised, and applicable with sufficient confidence. Unresolved availability must trigger a defined hold, safe alternative, or degraded path.
exclusions: The control is known to be available but is not activated.
The control's owner is uncertain while its operational availability remains clear.
The control operates and the dispute concerns whether its rule is adequate.
examples: An agent cannot determine whether the approval service governing a high-impact action is active in the current environment.
A workflow reaches execution without knowing whether the required policy control covers the selected tool path.

relationships.note: Control availability concerns whether a governance mechanism can operate; capability-authority conflation concerns treating operational ability as sufficient permission to act.
Availability ambiguity occurs before activation; control-state preservation begins only after operative control state exists.

VIGIL-FC-000037.failure_condition: A failure in which the operational availability, applicable coverage, or callable state of a required governance control cannot be determined with sufficient confidence before the control must influence a material decision or action.
VIGIL-FC-000037.failure_plain_english: It is materially unclear whether the governance control needed for a decision or action is available to operate.

required_conditions: A governance control may be required for a material decision or action.
Its operational availability or applicable coverage cannot be determined in time to rely on it.
The ambiguity materially impairs safe routing, activation, or execution.

VIGIL-FC-000037.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Availability and callable coverage are determined adequately before dependence, or the action enters a defined hold or safe alternative.

required_conditions: A material action depends on an applicable governance control whose availability may be uncertain.
Availability and callable coverage are determined adequately before dependence, or the action enters a defined hold or safe alternative.
Control checks and action records show the established availability or the actual bounded response to unresolved availability.

VIGIL-FC-000038.name: Required Control Activation
VIGIL-FC-000038.plain_english: An available, applicable control becomes operative when its valid trigger occurs, before the governed action proceeds.
VIGIL-FC-000038.definition: The property by which an available and applicable governance control is invoked, engaged and made operative when its defined valid trigger or required activation condition occurs, with the activation decision and resulting state observable and preserved.
VIGIL-FC-000038.invariant: When a valid activation condition is satisfied, the available applicable control must become operative before the governed action proceeds, and the activation decision and resulting state must be observable and preserved.
exclusions: The control activates but is bypassed downstream.
It is unresolved whether the control is available or applicable.
The triggering condition did not occur.
examples: A high-impact threshold is met, but the configured human-approval gate is never invoked.
A model change qualifies for required evaluation, yet the evaluation workflow is not activated before deployment.

relationships.note: Non-activation means no operative safeguard state is produced; a delivery dead-end means an operative governance signal is produced but fails to reach a capable endpoint.

Required non-activation occurs when valid activation conditions are satisfied but the control remains inactive; unwarranted activation occurs when those conditions are not satisfied but the control becomes operative.

subtypes.name: Control Authority Suppression
subtypes.plain_english: A control is present, but the force that should let it stop or redirect the action is disabled or neutralised.
subtypes.definition: A required-control-non-activation variant in which a governance control is reached or nominally present but its operative blocking, gating, escalation, or redirection authority is suppressed before it can govern the material action.

required_conditions: A governance control is applicable and nominally present or reached.
The control requires operative authority to block, gate, escalate, or redirect a material action.
That authority is disabled, neutralised, or withheld so the control cannot activate effectively.

exclusions: The control operates with authority but its substantive decision is disputed.
The actor never reaches the control because a required route is bypassed.
The issue is uncertainty about which actor has authority rather than suppression of the control's operative force.
examples: A safety gate receives a prohibited-action signal but is configured in advisory-only mode where blocking is required.
An escalation control is invoked, but its ability to pause execution is disabled for the active runtime.

VIGIL-FC-000083.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity
VIGIL-FC-000083.plain_english: A validly activated safeguard provides timely and sufficient protection for the hazard and evidenced protection needs in context.
VIGIL-FC-000083.definition: The property by which an applicable, validly activated governance or protective control produces an effect sufficient and timely to prevent, contain, interrupt, redirect, mitigate or safely bound its governed hazard to the level required by its protective purpose and evidenced protection context. Heightened protection conditions require evidence; disability or neurodivergence alone does not establish incapacity.
VIGIL-FC-000083.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
exclusions: The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.
The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.
The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.
Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.
examples: A content-safety control identifies an output as outside applicable guidelines and displays a warning, but the same harmful content remains visible to a protected user where the control's protective purpose requires prevention or containment.

A protective transaction or safety control activates and generates an advisory state, but the resulting effect is too late or too weak to satisfy the control's established containment or interruption requirement.

relationships.note: Required Control Activation asks whether an applicable control became operative when required; Control Effectiveness Integrity applies after valid activation and asks whether the resulting protective effect was materially sufficient.
Control Activation Validity asks whether the control should have activated; Control Effectiveness Integrity assumes valid activation and evaluates the sufficiency of the resulting protective effect.

Control-State Preservation concerns loss or weakening of an operative control state across a downstream transition; Control Effectiveness Integrity concerns an operative control whose realised effect is itself insufficient at the governed point.

Governance-signal delivery failure concerns an operative signal that cannot reach a capable endpoint; Control Effectiveness Integrity concerns a control that does operate at the governed point but does not achieve the protective effect required there.

VIGIL-FC-000083.failure_condition: A failure in which an applicable governance or protective control validly becomes operative, but the control effect it produces is materially insufficient to prevent, contain, interrupt, redirect, mitigate, or safely bound the governed hazard to the level required by the control's protective purpose and the evidenced protection context.
VIGIL-FC-000083.failure_plain_english: A protective control turns on, but the protection it actually provides is too weak, late, incomplete, or otherwise insufficient for the hazard it is meant to control.

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.

VIGIL-FC-000083.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.

required_conditions: An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.

VIGIL-FC-000072.name: Oversight Independence
VIGIL-FC-000072.plain_english: An oversight function retains the independence and practical capacity it needs to examine and challenge the conduct it reviews.
VIGIL-FC-000072.definition: The property by which a governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics or oversight function represented or relied upon as independent retains independence from interested or implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence continuity and protected escalation for material review and challenge.
VIGIL-FC-000072.invariant: A review function represented or relied upon as independent must retain practical independence from implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting capacity, evidence continuity, and protected escalation ability to test and challenge the conduct it oversees.
exclusions: The review function remains practically independent and adequately capable, even though it reaches an adverse or contested conclusion.
A governance signal merely fails to reach a capable review point without evidence that review independence or neutrality was impaired; assess Governance Signal Delivery.
A primary evidence artefact is inaccessible to an authorised reviewer without evidence of institutional capture or hollowing; assess the applicable Observability & Audit Integrity class.
An applicable control fails to activate, but the independence and practical capacity of the review function remain intact.
A monitor is evaded so consequential conduct can continue outside effective coverage; assess Monitoring Coverage Integrity.
The evidence establishes only inadequate performance, delay, disagreement, or resource scarcity without the required interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical impairment mechanism.
examples: A company publicly relies on an independent safety board while executives control its membership, evidence access, staffing and publication rights for reviews concerning those executives' own programme.
An oversight committee remains formally constituted but loses the mandate, technical access and protected reporting channel needed to challenge a material deployment decision.

relationships.note: A hollowed oversight function may also suppress or retaliate against a specific good-faith concern, but neither mechanism is required for the other.

Primary Evidence Accessibility concerns access to an authoritative artefact. Oversight Independence requires impairment of the review function's institutional independence or practical capacity by interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical authority.

invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The loss of evaluator access materially tests oversight independence and practical review capacity, but the evidence does not show institutional capture or that AISI's function was represented as effective while being hollowed.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: A review function represented or relied upon as independent must retain practical independence from implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting capacity, evidence continuity, and protected escalation ability to test and challenge the conduct it oversees.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The occurrence materially tests this class boundary without establishing all conditions needed to treat it as a failure occurrence or as successful holding.
boundary_conditions: Limited to the evidence and role adjudicated in the linked Incident.
Does not alter other Incident mappings or establish legal liability.

governance_placement.framework: The Institute of Internal Auditors
governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative analytical placement using a reference already retained by VIGIL-FC-000072; the referenced source does not define the VIGIL adjudication role.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts and provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000109; this entry records only the reciprocal taxonomy relationship.

VIGIL-FC-000072.failure_condition: A failure in which a governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is represented as independent or effective while an interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchically dominant authority materially compromises the function's independence or practical review capacity through control of appointment, removal, mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence preservation, escalation, or disposition.
VIGIL-FC-000072.failure_plain_english: An oversight body still exists on paper, but its independence or practical ability to examine and challenge material conduct has been stripped away.

required_conditions: A material governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is required or represented as capable of independent review.
An actor or institution with a material interest in, implication in, or hierarchical authority over the reviewed matter can influence the review function.
That influence materially impairs the function's independence, mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence preservation, escalation, or disposition capacity.
The function remains represented, relied upon, or treated as effective despite the impairment.
The impairment prevents or materially degrades independent testing, challenge, review, or disposition of the governed matter.

VIGIL-FC-000072.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: It retains practical mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting, evidence continuity and protected escalation sufficient for the affected review.

required_conditions: An independent oversight function reviews an interested or implicated actor.
It retains practical mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting, evidence continuity and protected escalation sufficient for the affected review.
Actual review and challenge evidence substantiates independence and capability for that matter rather than nominal institutional designation.
